newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti has "better" offer for PC company - paper.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti has "better" offer for PC company - paper.

text.p: Italy's troubled information technology Olivetti on Thursday was said to have frozen talks with British-based Klesch & Co over the sale of its ailing personal computer company, in favour of a "better" offer.
Milan financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore said that talks between Olivetti and Klesch, which specialises in defaulted corporate debt and is run by U.S. debt trader Gary Klesch, had been curtailed.
The paper reported that Olivetti's vice chairman Giorgio Garuzzo said the company "had received a better offer" for the PC company, which Olivetti hopes to sell by the end of the year.
An Olivetti spokesman declined to comment on any potential talks with any prospective buyers until a deal is completed, or even clarify Garuzzo's comments.
"No names, no comment until the deal is done," he said.
Klesch said in September that it may have looked at various parts of Olivetti, but it declined to confirm that it was considering any type of bid.
The PC company has long been a thorn in the side of Olivetti, losing 200 billion lire ($132 million) in 1995, and some 15.8 billion in the first half of 1996.

Previous management at Olivetti had hoped to bring the company back to breakeven in 1996, but chief executive Roberto Colaninno, who took over in September, said the aim was to sell off the PC company by the end of the year.

Il Sole said the Olivetti talks were with Klesch and U.S. financier Bennet Lebow. These two groups had agreed to leave Bernard Auer as the head of PCs and maintain production and jobs at the PCs base at Scarmagno, near Ivrea in northwest Italy.
In return, Olivetti's Systems and Services company would agree to buy around 50 percent of sales from the PC company, the paper added.
At 1225 GMT, Olivetti shares were 6.15 percent up at 540 lire on the Milan stock market after surging to a session high of 543. It was the most traded stock in volume of nearly 28 million shares.
